question.text: Copper sulphate solution <math> <mrow> <mtext>(250</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>mL)</mtext></mrow> </math> was electrolysed using a platinum anode and a copper cathode. A constant current of <math> <mrow> <mtext>2</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>mA</mtext></mrow> </math> was passed for <math> <mrow> <mtext>16</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>min</mtext></mrow> </math>. It was found that after electrolysis the absorbance of the solution was reduced to <math> <mrow> <mtext>50%</mtext></mrow> </math> of its original value. Concentration of copper sulphate in the solution to begin with is <math><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Find the valu of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math>

solution.text:
The number of faraday's passed = 2 × 1 0 - 3 × 1 6 × 6 0 9 6 5 0 0

                                                      = 1.99 × 1 0 - 5

⇒ number of gram equivalent of Cu 2 + deposited as Cu(s)

                                                = 1.99 × 1 0 - 5

⇒ number of moles of Cu 2 + deposited

                          = 1.99 2 × 10 - 5 ≈ 10 - 5

Absorbance is directly proportional to Cu 2 + .

No. of moles of Cu2+ initially present = 2 x 10-5 moles

Cu 2 + Initial = 2 × 1 0 - 5 × 1 0 0 0 2 5 0

                   = 8 x10-5M
